meta.title: South African K53 Light Motor Vehicle Study Pack
meta.target: South African light motor vehicle learner's licence
meta.source_policy: NaTIS/Department of Transport manuals are primary; current government service pages used for administrative facts.

question_bank.q: What is the general speed limit on a public road in an urban area unless another limit is shown?
question_bank.why: The general urban limit is 60 km/h.

question_bank.q: What is the general speed limit on a non-freeway public road outside an urban area unless another limit is shown?
question_bank.why: The general non-freeway limit outside an urban area is 100 km/h.

question_bank.q: What is the general speed limit on a freeway unless another limit is shown?
question_bank.why: The general freeway limit is 120 km/h.

question_bank.q: When overtaking a vehicle travelling in the same direction, you normally pass it on:
question_bank.why: The normal rule is to pass on the right.

question_bank.q: May you exceed the speed limit while overtaking?
question_bank.why: The speed limit still applies while overtaking.

question_bank.q: A green traffic light allows you to enter an intersection when:
options: The light is green regardless of congestion
There is enough space to clear the intersection
question_bank.why: Do not block an intersection.

question_bank.q: At a traffic circle, unless another control applies, you should yield to:
options: Traffic approaching from your right within the circle
question_bank.why: The learner manual states traffic in the circle from the right has priority unless controlled otherwise.

question_bank.q: Before changing lanes you should:
options: Check mirrors, blind spot and safe gap
question_bank.why: Observation and a safe gap are essential.

question_bank.q: A road shoulder is:
question_bank.why: Shoulder use is limited and conditional.

question_bank.q: If road conditions are poor, you should:
options: Always drive at the posted limit
Reduce speed to a safe speed
question_bank.why: The legal maximum may still be unsafe.

question_bank.q: A learner driving a car must normally be accompanied by:
options: A person licensed to drive the relevant class
question_bank.why: A licensed supervising driver is required.

question_bank.q: What does an indicator give you?
question_bank.why: Signals do not create priority.

question_bank.q: If you are involved in a collision, your first legal/safety duty includes:
options: Driving away if the car still moves
question_bank.why: A driver involved in a crash must stop.

question_bank.q: When parking, you should:
options: Avoid obstructing traffic and obey signs/markings
Park partly on the pavement whenever convenient
question_bank.why: Parking must not create danger or contravene controls.

question_bank.q: Stopping on a freeway is normally:
options: Prohibited except in limited lawful circumstances
question_bank.why: Freeway stopping is tightly restricted.

question_bank.q: Pedal cycles on a freeway are:
options: Always allowed in the emergency lane
question_bank.why: Pedal cycles are among vehicles prohibited on freeways.

question_bank.q: A hand-held mobile phone while driving should be:
question_bank.why: Hand-held use while driving is prohibited.

question_bank.q: High beam should be dipped when:
options: It could dazzle another road user
question_bank.why: Do not dazzle other road users.

question_bank.q: The hooter is primarily used to:
question_bank.why: It is a warning device.

question_bank.q: A safe following gap should:
options: Stay the same in all weather
question_bank.why: Poor conditions require more stopping space.

question_bank.q: When turning, you should:
options: Observe, signal, position and yield as required
question_bank.why: Turning requires observation, signalling and correct positioning.

question_bank.q: A traffic officer signals you to proceed even though a normal sign would stop you. You should:
question_bank.why: Lawful directions by traffic officers take precedence.

question_bank.q: A load carried by a vehicle must:
options: Obstruct the driver’s view if tied down
question_bank.why: Loads must not create danger.

question_bank.q: Driving recklessly or negligently is:
question_bank.why: Reckless/negligent driving is prohibited.

question_bank.q: When another vehicle is merging from an on-ramp on a freeway, you should:
question_bank.why: Safe merging requires cooperation and space.

question_bank.q: A speed-limit sign showing 80 means:
options: You may not exceed 80 while it applies
question_bank.why: It sets a maximum.

question_bank.q: If you cannot see enough clear road ahead to overtake safely, you should:
question_bank.why: Never overtake blindly.

question_bank.q: Seat belts fitted to a vehicle should:
question_bank.why: Seat belts are a core occupant-safety requirement.

question_bank.q: An octagonal red sign means:
question_bank.why: STOP is the major octagonal exception to the usual round regulatory shape.

question_bank.q: A triangular sign with a red border normally indicates:
question_bank.why: Warning signs are generally triangular.

question_bank.q: A round regulatory sign primarily:
question_bank.why: Regulatory signs tell you what you must/must not do.

question_bank.q: A YIELD sign requires you to:
options: Give priority and stop if necessary
question_bank.why: Yield does not always require a full stop.

question_bank.q: A NO ENTRY sign means:
options: Do not enter from that direction
question_bank.why: Entry is prohibited.

question_bank.q: A NO U-TURN sign means:
question_bank.why: The manoeuvre is prohibited.

question_bank.q: A KEEP LEFT sign requires you to:
options: Pass the obstruction on the left
question_bank.why: It is a command sign.

question_bank.q: A warning sign showing pedestrians means you should:
options: Reduce speed and watch for pedestrians
question_bank.why: Prepare for a pedestrian hazard.

question_bank.q: A slippery-road warning means you should:
options: Reduce speed and avoid sudden inputs
question_bank.why: Smooth control reduces loss of grip.

question_bank.q: A sign warning of traffic signals ahead tells you to:
question_bank.why: The warning prepares you for signal control.

question_bank.q: A broken lane line may normally be crossed:
question_bank.why: Broken lines permit lane changes when safe.

question_bank.q: A solid barrier line generally means:
question_bank.why: It restricts crossing.

question_bank.q: At a stop line with a red traffic light you should stop:
question_bank.why: Stop before the line.

question_bank.q: A yield line tells you to:
options: Give way and stop if necessary
question_bank.why: It marks the give-way point.

question_bank.q: A painted island is an area you should normally:
options: Not drive, stop or park on
question_bank.why: It separates/protects traffic space.

question_bank.q: A parking bay marking means:
question_bank.why: Keep the vehicle within the marked area.

question_bank.q: A steady red traffic light means:
question_bank.why: Red requires stopping.

question_bank.q: A steady green light means:
options: Proceed only if the way is clear
question_bank.why: Green does not cancel other safety duties.

question_bank.q: An amber/yellow traffic light means:
options: Stop if you can do so safely
question_bank.why: Do not rush the signal.

question_bank.q: A green arrow allows movement:
options: In the arrow direction when safe
question_bank.why: It applies to the shown direction.

question_bank.q: Guidance signs are mainly used to:
question_bank.why: Guidance helps navigation.

question_bank.q: Information signs mainly:
question_bank.why: They inform rather than command.

question_bank.q: Roadworks signs mean you should:
options: Expect changed conditions and obey temporary control
question_bank.why: Temporary conditions require extra caution.

question_bank.q: A road marking nearest your vehicle in a combination line is important because:
options: It determines whether crossing is allowed from your side
Both lines can always be crossed
question_bank.why: Your side of the combination governs your movement.

question_bank.q: A yellow edge line marks:
options: The left edge of the roadway
question_bank.why: It commonly marks the roadway edge.

question_bank.q: A pedestrian crossing marking means you should:
options: Keep the crossing clear and yield/stop as required
question_bank.why: Pedestrian crossings must not be blocked.

question_bank.q: Directional arrows painted in a lane:
question_bank.why: Lane arrows guide/require movement.

question_bank.q: A NO STOPPING restriction is generally:
options: The same as a speed limit
question_bank.why: No stopping prevents even brief stops except lawful exceptions.

question_bank.q: Which control changes the vehicle’s direction?
question_bank.why: The steering wheel controls direction.

question_bank.q: Which pedal normally slows/stops the vehicle?
question_bank.why: The foot/service brake slows or stops.

question_bank.q: In a manual car, the clutch is used mainly to:
options: Disconnect/connect engine drive for gear changes/moving off
question_bank.why: The clutch connects/disconnects drive.

question_bank.q: Which control holds the car stationary when parked?
question_bank.why: The parking brake secures a stationary vehicle.

question_bank.q: Which instrument shows road speed?
question_bank.why: The speedometer shows road speed.

question_bank.q: Which control warns other road users of your intention to turn?
question_bank.why: Indicators communicate turning/lateral intention.

question_bank.q: Which device helps clear rain from the windscreen?
question_bank.why: Wipers clear the windscreen.

question_bank.q: Mirrors do not remove the need to check:
question_bank.why: Blind spots can hide road users.
